Posted March 13, 2004
Analysis by Richard Cowan

Last month, John Walters crowed that teen marijuana use was declining, and this proved that the Drug War is enjoying yet one more great victory. The occasion was the latest survey (PATS Study 2003 Teens) by The Partnership For A Drug-Free America, which claimed that over the past five years, there had been a seven percent decline (from 42 to 39 percent in one-time teen marijuana use.)

Then we are told, If the decline had not occurred, 760,000 more teens would have tried marijuana than is currently the case. "

T was a great victory. Sort if like Iraq. Give or take a bit

However, for once the margin of error in the survey was not hidden. It was right there for everyone to ignore: " The margin of error for the sample is +/1.5 percent. "
(In pollster-speak that means that 95% of the time the numbers will be accurate within that range. Generally speaking, the larger the sample, the smaller the margin of error will be, but there are other questions about the accuracy of polls on illicit or unpopular activities.)

Thus, the " seven percent decline (from 42 to 39 percent) " claimed for marijuana is actually just three percentage points, which is exactly the plus or minus 1.5% margin of error. So there may not have been any change at all.
(For example, a drop from 10% to 8% is two percentage points, but a 20% change. If the margin of error is greater than difference, then the numbers may not mean anything at all. Watch for the margin of errors in the Presidential polls.)

The media has been going along with this for years.
From 2000, see
Again the Media Parrots the Partnership's Prohibitionist Propaganda Even Though Reported " Changes " Are Within the Margin of Error. Emphasis in Propaganda as in Seizures Shows Drug War Really About Marijuana

The prohibitionists know that they can count on the incompetence or the ideological commitment to prohibition by journalists and editorial writers to keep them from questioning what they are reading.

Thus, over a five-year period, more than 3 million Americans of all ages were arrested on marijuana charges to prevent a possible 760,000 teens from trying marijuana once. The 3 million are real. The 760,000 are speculative.
See
NORML Reports Marijuana Arrests For 2002 Near Record High Pot Smokers Arrested In America At A Rate Of One Every 45 Seconds Plus Analysis by Richard Cowan.
and
NORML Study Reveals Blacks Arrested For Marijuana At More Than Twice The Rate For Whites

However, on March 10th USA Today did its duty to the fatherland and carried an Op-ed by John Walters, Goal is to halt abusein which he proclaimed:
Prescription drug abuse is the second largest illicit drug problem in America only marijuana is more widely abused. In fact, 6.2 million Americans reported abuse of these drugs last year, while one in 10 high school seniors admitted abuse of a single brand of prescription narcotic: Vicodin. The number of people abusing OxyContin has doubled every year since we first asked the question on national surveys and now is approaching the number who have abused heroin while the addictive potential is comparable.
See
The Spin Is Beginning To Wobble On The " Latest Teen Drug Use " Survey. Czar Is " Greatly Encouraged " By Poll Showing Heroin Use By 12th Graders At All Time High.

In 2003, about one in ten also reported " abuse " of Ritalin or Adderall without a doctor's prescription.

Of course, the immediate purpose of this new program is to escalate the war on pain patients and their doctors.
See
What Is More Important, Prohibition Or The Patients? The Death of Cheryl Miller Should Remind Us All To Demand A Change In Priorities. Should Pain Be A Crime?
and
Bennett, Limbaugh, and the Blindness of the Prohibitionist Paradigm.
and
Live Free or Die In Pain. The Ignorance and Arrogance of the Quacks Who Deny Pain Relief to the Sick and Dying.

According to NIDA, in the mid-1980s, fewer than 500,000 reported they used painkillers for non-medical reasons; in 1998, 1.6 million people were taking them.

On October 9, 2003, The Christian Science Monitor, reported that between 1995 and 2002, there was a 163 percent increase in the number of emergency-room visits tied to the abuse of prescription drugs, according to the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Agency. Prescription drugs are now a factor in a quarter of all overdose deaths reported in the United States.

The Florida Department of Law Enforcement reported that, in 2000, in just that one state, 152 deaths were blamed on oxycodone and hydrocodone - - the ingredients in OxyContin and Vicodan. And 93 deaths were attributed to benzodiazepines, tranquilizers likeValium and Xanax, Noelle Bush's drug. (Women are two to three times more likely to be diagnosed with depression and prescribed such drugs.)
See
Cannabis Prohibition Prostitutes Science In New Emergency Dept. Data. Hiding the Truth Behind A Cloud of Lies.

One may wonder how his Czarship can claim that marijuana use is a bigger problem that Vicodin and Oxycontin use. But that is another subject.
See
Walters Tells a New Lie. Oh Happy Day! People Need Treatment If They Are Sent to Treatment, By Definition. And How Do They Treat Marijuana Addicts? We Couldn't Make This Up, But They Did.

Instead, let's examine the rest of the problem of the misuse of both prescription and non-prescription drugs.

For example, DXM a synthetic version of codeine found in more than 100 non-prescription cold remedies seems to be highly addictive. It is estimated that half of the teens in rehabilitation programs for DXM leave early. Only 20 percent stay clean for a year. In the past two years, 14 children nationwide have died from overdosing on DXM. Hundreds more were hospitalized. It is also a serious problem in the UK.
See
Marijuana Isn't Harmless. Okay, But Why Isn't It Sold Over the Counter? Or Would You Ban Something That Causes 300,000 ER Visits Every Year, And Kills A Child Every Month? (Trick Question)
and
Meanwhile UK Painkillers Kill 2,000 Per Year. But They Are Sold Over-the-Counter So They Must Be Safe!
and
Two More Stories from The UK That We Couldn't Make Up: 10,000 Scots Addicted To Dangerous Over-The-Counter Drugs and Bristol Police Drunk and Lewd At Anti-Drug Benefit.

Of course, prescription drugs can be even more dangerous, but it is not just their illegal diversion that is problem. There are some very serious questions about the over-prescribing of pharmaceuticals for children and adolescents as well as adults.
See
California Caretakers " Routinely Drug Foster Children; " Great Journalism;
We Are All Kept In A Chemical Straightjacket
and
DEAland Children Consume 90% of the World's Ritalin. " This year six million children across the USA -- over one tenth of the schoolage population -- will be prescribed anti-depressants and stimulants. " Context for The Medical Marijuana Debate and " Drug Education "

On October 23, 2001, The New York Times reported:
FAMILIES SUE DRUG MAKER Families of some victims of the 1999 Columbine High School shootings have sued the maker of the antidepressant drug Luvox, which one of the gunmen, Eric Harris, had been taking. An autopsy revealed a therapeutic amount of the drug in Mr. Harris. The relatives of five of the victims claim that the drug maker, Solvay Pharmaceuticals, did not adequately warn Mr. Harris's psychiatrist about the drug's side effects, which may include impaired judgment. Two of the victims whose families are involved in the suit died, and three were wounded. The families seek $75,000 each.
See
Georgia Shooter Was On Ritalin: " We have no reason to believe that was (the cause). "
What If It Had Been Marijuana?
and
What If the Colorado Shooter Had Been Using Marijuana Instead Of A Pharmaceutical?
Two Different Standards.

October 24, 2001, USA TODAY reported:Doctors are increasingly prescribing psychiatric drugs such as Ritalin and Prozac to preschoolers, despite questions about safety and effectiveness, experts reported over the weekend.

Nobody knows exactly how many preschool children are on psychiatric drugs. Some evidence suggests it's only a few out of every 100 youngsters. But concern has been mounting since a report last year showed that Ritalin use more than tripled in preschoolers between 1991 and 1995, and prescriptions for antidepressants doubled in that age group during the same period.

Many of the problems described above are directly or indirectly a result of cannabis prohibition, and especially the suppression of medical cannabis with the full support of organized quackery. It is made all the more obscene by the claim that it is being done to protect children.
See
How the War On Marijuana To Save The Children
Has Become A War On the Children To Save Marijuana Prohibition
and
No, Cannabis Will Not Be The 21st Century Aspirin Because It Doesn't Kill Anyone! People Suffer And Die, While Scientists Try To Pharmaceuticalize The Aspirin Of the 21st Century B.C.
and
Science, Democracy, Ideology and the Prohibitionist Police State. Marijuana Use Doesn't Hurt Thinking Skills But Prohibition Does. Analysis by Richard Cowan
and
Calling All Quacks: The Therapeutic Police State and the Politicization of Medicine. Doctors Cannot Study The Violence of Cannabis Prohibition. Because They Are The Disease, Not The Cure.
